themes_detail.label: Dead animals piling up
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 10 this week, a 515% jump from the 8-week average of 1.6 per week (z-score: 5.31), signaling a possible sanitation crisis or environmental health hazard affecting Upper East Side residents.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (515% spike)
Z-score of 5.31 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Suggests potential public health concern or inadequate animal removal services
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if dead animal pickup is delayed or if there's an environmental trigger (disease, food source proliferation)
Interview residents on affected blocks; document locations and timeline of complaints

themes_detail.label: Litter baskets overflowing
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints jumped to 3 this week versus 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42), suggesting inadequate sanitation infrastructure or collection gaps in Upper East Side neighborhoods.
evidence: 3 litter basket complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Part of broader sanitation concerns alongside dead animal spike
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify if specific neighborhoods or commercial corridors are under-serviced
Request DSNY collection schedules and staffing levels for this district

themes_detail.label: Park rules violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violations spiked to 5 complaints two weeks ago, a 900% jump from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 per week (z-score: 9.0, highest severity), pointing to possible enforcement gaps or emerging park safety/quality issues.
evidence: 5 park rules violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike)
Z-score of 9.0 (highest statistical severity among all spikes)
Suggests concentrated enforcement issue or behavioral shift in major parks (likely Central Park, Madison Square Park)
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated complaints; interview Parks Dept. on enforcement staffing and recent incidents
Speak with park regulars and nearby residents about what rule-breaking activity they've observed

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure crumbling
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints surged to 9 last week (800% spike from 1.0 weekly average, z-score: 8.0) and street sign missing complaints reached 7 two weeks ago (460% spike from 1.2 weekly average, z-score: 5.94), indicating accelerating deterioration of navigation infrastructure.
evidence: Street sign damage: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (800% spike, z-score: 8.0)
Street sign missing: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (460% spike, z-score: 5.94)
DOT budget request for 'repair or build new step streets' suggests long-standing infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Request DOT maintenance schedules and budget allocations for CD 108; compare to other districts
Document specific intersections with missing/damaged signs; photograph conditions and interview residents about safety impacts (pedestrian, traffic)

themes_detail.label: Abandoned vehicles accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped to 8 last week, a 276% spike from the 2.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.58), suggesting possible increase in vehicle dumping or inadequate enforcement sweeps.
evidence: 8 abandoned vehicle complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (276% spike)
Z-score of 5.58 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Suggests either organized dumping or reduced NYPD/DSNY enforcement of vehicle removal
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and DSNY to determine if there are specific blocks or neighborhoods with concentration; request removal timelines
Interview residents on affected streets about whether they've noticed patterns or suspect illegal dumping
